stem.text: Find the particular solution to the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = \sin{\left(x^{2} \right)} \) with the initial condition \( y(1) = -1 \), written in terms of a definite integral.

worked_solution.text: The right side depends on x alone and has no elementary antiderivative, so accumulate it from the initial input: \( \int_{1}^{x} \sin{\left(t^{2} \right)}\,dt \) is the change in y from x = 1.
Add the initial value: \( y = -1 + \int_{1}^{x} \sin{\left(t^{2} \right)}\,dt \), which equals \( -1 \) at x = 1 and has derivative \( \sin{\left(x^{2} \right)} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: initial value plus the accumulated change

options.label: \( y = -1 + \int_{1}^{x} \sin{\left(t^{2} \right)} \)
options.derivation: the initial value and the integral written with the differential dt left off

options.label: \( y = \int_{1}^{x} \sin{\left(t^{2} \right)}\,dt \)
options.derivation: the accumulated change written alone, without the initial value

options.label: \( y = \sin{\left(x^{2} \right)} - 1 - \sin{\left(1 \right)} \)
options.derivation: the given rate treated as though it were the quantity itself, shifted to pass through the initial point
